thread:
maria: quick datapoint from an overnight run: host-side parse + grpc streaming for the long-chat scenario is consuming a lot more CPU than expected. tokenization + framing are hot when streaming and requests hit ~1.2k tokens (looks like ~30-40% CPU). :chart_with_upwards_trend:
aj: can you drop the sampled flame and top counts?
maria: pasted short stack summary:
```
Top CPU contributors (sampled):
- host::tokenize           34.7%
- host::stream_frame       19.1%
- proto::unpack            11.7%
- kvcache::check_hit       7.9%
- kernel_selector          6.8%
- allocator::malloc        4.2%
```
This was with kernel_hint="auto", batch_target=16, kv_hit ~62% (cold start from canary).
aj: 62% KV hit is surprising for chat. Are small streaming fragments causing repeated parse/unpack?
maria: yep. traces show many tiny fragments (~100-300B) that run the full parse path and trigger allocations each time. cumulative cost is heavy.
sam: that aligns with the stream microbench. Two quick mitigations: reuse a proto arena (avoid per-frag allocs) and coalesce small upstream writes so the parser sees fewer, larger frames.
maria: implemented a local arena in the proto unpacker and re-ran: allocs during parse dropped ~42%, tokenize CPU down ~18% on a synthetic 1k token run. also experimented with forcing kernel_hint="smallseq" on the host and caching kernel selection per-session.
aj: caching hint per-session makes sense; switching kernel_select every request is branching overhead. maybe compute kernel choice on first request and keep until sequence-length delta > 256?
maria: implemented session-kernel-cache with invalidation when seq_len jumps by >256. cheap to add. preliminary runs show kernel_selector CPU portion down ~60%.
aj: scheduler side: when kv_hit < 70% bias to smaller batch_target to reduce wasted compute from misses. can we add a short-circuit to the scheduler?
sam: also look at ingress write syscall churn. enabling writev/coalesce at proxy for streaming reduces syscall rate. but watch tail latency.
infra-bot: deploy queued: perf-preflight build 0.11.3-preflight -> canary host-pool-4 (requested by maria).
mara: (typo) will run canary. planned changes: 1) proto arena unpack, 2) session kernel cache + invalidation, 3) ingress coalesce threshold adjust (coalesce small writes up to 1kb or 20ms), 4) scheduler kv-hit sliding window that sets batch_target=8 when <70%.
nora: add metrics: kv_hit_ratio, token_cpu_per_sec, tokens_per_sec, p50/p95 token-latency. dashboard panels please.
maria: will add. early local test: kv warmup via synthetic priming bumped hit to 78%; overall token CPU/sec improved ~22% on long-chat load.
aj: for proxy coalesce, do adaptive flush: coalesce up to 1kb or 20ms, but flush immediately on end-of-chunk indicators to keep interactivity.
sam: prototype of writev coalesce looks promising locally. dropping syscall churn reduces host CPU for small writes by ~12%.
infra-bot: canary deploy perf-preflight -> host-pool-4 succeeded in 3m.
maria: running 30m canary collection now. will post p50/p95 diffs and traces.
nora: next steps and owners: maria -> land proto-arena + session-kernel-cache + coalesce prototype (INF-4821), aj -> add scheduler kv-window + batching thresholds (INF-4822), sam -> proxy adaptive writev patch (INF-4823). add Grafana panels and alert thresholds.
aj: once 30m canary traces in, share the diff for token-latency and token-CPU/sec. want to see behavior under bursts. :thumbsup:
maria: will follow up with traces and attached flame graphs. thanks!
sam: LGTM
